t.5.1: Hear, O fair-thighed one, of the season called Śiśira, when the earth is covered with heaps of ripened rice and sugarcane and graced here and there by the cries of resting krauñca birds, a season full of abundant desire and dear to young women.
t.5.3: Neither sandal paste cool as the rays of the moon, nor the palace rooftop bright as the autumn moon, nor winds cold with dense frost delight people's hearts now.
t.5.2: The interiors of houses with their windows shut, fire, the rays of the sun, heavy garments, and women in the bloom of youth: in this season, these become what people seek out and enjoy.
t.5.4: Chilled by the falling of masses of frost, and made colder still by the rays of the moon, the nights, lovely in their ornament of pale clusters of stars, are not fit for people to enjoy.
t.5.5: Having taken betel, unguents and garlands, their lotus-faces fragrant with flower-wine, eager women enter the bedchamber richly perfumed with the smoke of black aloe-wood incense.
t.5.6: Seeing their husbands, who had often committed offences and been sharply rebuked, now trembling, their minds lost in fear, yet longing for love's union, the women, flushed with wine, forgot their offences.
t.5.7: Young women in the fresh bloom of youth, long and pitilessly enjoyed through the lengthy nights by young men of unbounded desire, wander slowly at the night's end, their thighs aching with weariness.
t.5.8: Women, their breasts pressed by charming bodices, their thighs adorned with richly dyed silks, and with flowers set within their tresses, seem to adorn the coming of winter.
t.5.9: Their chests pressed close by playful women with breasts tawny-red from the tint of saffron, pleasant to embrace and warm with the heat of fresh youth, lovers sleep on, disdaining the cold.
t.5.10: At night, delighted, women drink with their lovers the finest intoxicating wine, charming and awakening desire and the delight of love, its lotus trembling under their fragrant breath.
t.5.11: At daybreak a young woman, her intoxication and passion now spent, the tips of her breasts pressed close by her husband's embrace, gazes at her own body enjoyed by her dearest and goes laughing from the bedchamber to another room.
t.5.12: At dawn another passionate woman, heavy-hipped, deep-navelled and slender-waisted, leaves her bed, bearing her lovely, radiant mass of hair, perfumed with fragrant aloe-wood incense, its garland of flowers slipped away and its tips curled.
t.5.14: Other young women, weighed down by the burden of their broad hips, their waists slightly bowed, walking ever so slowly from the weariness of their heavy breasts, quickly cast off the night's attire suited to the hour of love and put on dress fit for the day.
t.5.13: At dawn, with their round faces lovely as golden lotuses, with charming copper-red lower lips, with eyes reaching to the edges of their ears and rosy at the corners, and with hair clinging to their shoulders, the women standing within the house today seem like so many goddesses of Fortune.
t.5.15: Gazing at the curves of their breasts covered with nail-marks, touching the tip of their bud-like lower lips bitten by teeth, and delighting in the guise of the lovemaking they had longed for, young women adorn their faces at the hour of sunrise.
t.5.16: Abounding in sweets made from molasses, delightful with sweet rice and sugarcane, full of ardent love-play, a season in which the pride of Kandarpa has arisen, yet a cause of mounting anguish for those parted from their beloved: may this winter season ever be for your welfare.
